scope: All units read: text for sense, translation and word glosses against the text. The text was not compared with the source page. The hymn is full of sound-play and several lines are obscure; where translation and word gloss disagreed I followed the construction the grammar supports.

items.issue: nandanute and jiṣṇunute were “praised by the blessed” and “by the victorious”; the word glosses had Nanda and Indra.
items.change: Translation now names Nanda and Jiṣṇu (Indra).

items.issue: Lines 2–3 were misconstrued: the trident is planted on the foes’ heads, and tigmakara is the sun, not “your fierce hand”.
items.change: Retranslated to agree with the word glosses.

items.issue: bhūtapate was taken as an address “O lord of the ghost-hosts”; the Goddess enchants Bhūtapati (Śiva). naṭārdha-naṭī-naṭa-nāyaka is Ardhanārīśvara as lord of dancers.

items.change: Now “O king's daughter, a very god of love to bewitch …”; word gloss of line 1 corrected (pate is “mistress”, not “gait”).

items.issue: sahasrakara is the thousand-rayed Sun who praises her; the translation had “thousand hands of the thousand-handed”. Line 2 likewise loosened.
items.change: Retranslated to agree with the word glosses.

items.issue: “a gleaming golden pitcher-sea” was not English or Sanskrit.
The moon-faced women of Indra’s city do not “outshine” her face; the devotee who courts her face is not turned away by them.
Word gloss had vadha-udita for the text’s vadhodyata.
The gloss named Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa though the page text reads khaṇḍa … muṇḍa.
items.change: Gloss now follows the page text and notes the other reading.

items.issue: Two misspellings in verse 13: tribhivanabhūṣaṇa (for tribhuvana) and mattamattaṃgaja (for mattamataṅgaja). The word glosses already have the right forms.
items.recommend: A: neither is a word as printed.

items.issue: Line 3 reads nipātitakhaṇḍavipātitamuṇḍa; most texts read nipātitacaṇḍa…, naming the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.
options: B. Change to caṇḍa and translate with the two demons’ names.
items.recommend: A unless your recitation text has caṇḍa; both are transmitted.

items.issue: Line 3 ends mukharīkṛtatigmakare (“who makes the sun resound”); the common text is mukharīkṛtadiṅmakare (“who fills the quarters with sound”).
options: B. Change to diṅmakare and retranslate.
items.recommend: A unless your recitation text differs.

items.issue: Verses 11, 12 and 19 (line 3) are sound-play whose sense is uncertain; translation and gloss give plausible but unverified renderings.
options: B. Mark them as tentative on the page.
C. You supply the sense from a commentary.
